*** THIS IS THE HIGHEST-RISK TASK IN EITHER PRD. BOTH APPS BLOCK ON IT AND ITS INTERFACE WAS NEGOTIATED WITH ANOTHER DESIGN SESSION. Implement the names exactly as given; do not rename or restructure them. ***

RESPONSIBILITY 2 -- THE RUN DATABASE. A PER-USER LOCAL DATABASE in the user's home directory, the single store both apps read and write.

   THE INTERFACE IS AGREED WITH THE SESSION DESIGNING THE SECOND APP. Implement these names exactly; another PRD is being written against them.

     class KorosArcStore:
         list_projects() -> list[ProjectRecord]
         list_arcs(project: str) -> list[ArcRecord]
         read_arc(project: str, arc: str) -> ArcRecord
         record_analysis(project, arc, record: AnalysisRecord) -> None
         list_analyses(project, arc, kind: str | None = None) -> list[AnalysisRecord]
         read_detail(record_id: str) -> dict

   AnalysisRecord fields: record_id (str, producer-generated; re-recording the same id REPLACES, never duplicates), kind (str, NAMESPACED e.g. 'kbdl.annotation', 'kbdl.skani', 'kbutillib.fba'), created_at (ISO8601 UTC), producer (str, tool + version), subject (str), status (str: ok|failed|partial), artifacts (dict of named refs to files/objects, NEVER inlined data), payload (dict, THE SEAM -- opaque here, never interpreted), trust_tier (str), provenance (dict), contract_version (int).

   *** THE TWO-TIER SCHEMA IS THE CRUX OF THIS TASK. GET IT RIGHT. ***
   - SQL COLUMNS carry only the NAVIGABLE dimensions: record_id, project, arc (both NULLABLE -- both null means unattributed), subject, kind, producer, status, trust_tier, timestamps, counts, and PRECOMPUTED SUMMARY STATISTICS such as a per-genome consistency figure. Roughly one row per run and one per subject-method pair. These are what the dashboard and arc views sort, filter and aggregate on.
   - JSON BLOBS carry gene-level and reaction-level detail, ONE BLOB PER SUBJECT (per genome). NEVER expand these into rows. The arithmetic: a 4,617-gene genome across up to fifteen methods is ~70,000 gene-level facts FOR ONE GENOME; as rows that is tens of millions across a corpus, as a blob it is one row.
   - read_detail is THE ONLY call that opens a blob. Keep that boundary visible in the API, not hidden in an implementation. list_analyses must never open one.
   - The database is ENABLED BY DEFAULT ON PODS and configurable elsewhere. Provide that configuration.

   ALSO ENFORCE HERE, not in either app:
   - The trust_tier enum has exactly four values, decreasing trust: verified, homology, hypothesis, opinion. Provide a comparison so callers can ask for 'homology-or-better'.
   - THE FLOOR RULE: a record summarizing several findings carries the FLOOR, the least-trusted contributing tier. Provide a floor helper. Adding lower-tier findings lowers the floor; adding higher-tier ones NEVER raises it.
   - ANTI-LAUNDERING: provide NO API that raises a tier. The floor helper is the only way a summary tier is produced.
   - Any tier other than verified REQUIRES a non-empty provenance dict carrying the bridge kind and its metric. Reject a write that omits it.
   - UNKNOWN-KIND POLICY, imitated from kbdl_service.clearinghouse.result_types: an unrecognized kind is STORED AND FLAGGED, never refused. Only a record failing structural validation is rejected. The second app writes its own kinds into this same database, so one unknown kind must never stall a reader. A foreign kind must be COUNTED, never silently dropped.


SEAM: payload is OPAQUE here -- typed but never interpreted. One app reads kbdl.annotation payloads, the other kbutillib.fba payloads. This module knows neither.

Follow KBUtilLib's existing conventions and test style. Tests must cover: empty inputs/tool_versions parsing as valid; a project with no arcs/ subdirectory enumerating as zero arcs; an unparseable PROVENANCE.json not breaking enumeration; the floor rule in both directions; a non-verified tier without provenance rejected; an unknown kind stored, flagged and counted rather than dropped; a null project/arc record stored and readable as unattributed; re-recording a record_id replacing rather than duplicating; read_detail returning the blob; AND -- most important -- that list_analyses and the summary queries open NO blob.


*** CONCRETE SPECIFICATIONS, folded from confront round 1. These are DECIDED -- implement them, do not re-derive. ***
ENGINE AND PATH: SQLite. Resolve from KBDL_RUN_DB if set, else ~/.kbdl/runs.sqlite. THE NAMES ARE DELIBERATELY DOMAIN-NEUTRAL because a second app (model analysis) shares this database -- do NOT name anything 'annotation' or 'genome' at the schema level.
TABLE runs: record_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, project TEXT NULL, arc_slug TEXT NULL, subject TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, producer TEXT NOT NULL, producer_version TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, trust_tier TEXT NOT NULL, provenance TEXT NOT NULL (JSON), contract_version INTEGER NOT NULL, unknown_kind INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL, subject_feature_count INTEGER, method_count INTEGER, consistency_overall REAL NULL, consistency_metric_version TEXT NULL, ic_corpus_version TEXT NULL.
TABLE subject_detail: record_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, detail_json TEXT NOT NULL. ONE ROW PER SUBJECT. This is the blob tier and the ONLY place gene-level or reaction-level data lives.
PROVENANCE JSON: { bridge_kind, metric: {name, value, units}, source: {db, accession} }. bridge_kind names the BRIDGE, NOT the tier -- one of id_join, sequence_homolog, profile_hmm, model_prediction, user_assertion. Do NOT use tier names here.
CONTRACT_VERSION IS AN INTEGER, currently 1. NOT a semver string -- the CAC rules it an integer explicitly and a string breaks interop with the peer apps.
UNKNOWN KINDS set unknown_kind=1, are stored, counted and badged, are never rejected, and are EXCLUDED from any consistency computation.
TEST FIXTURES under tests/fixtures/koros_arc_store/ with runs_db/ and subject_blobs/. No network in tests.

*** record_id AND artifacts, agreed with the session designing the second app. DECIDED. ***
record_id IS DERIVED BY ONE SHARED HELPER IN THIS MODULE, not by each producer -- otherwise the replace-never-duplicate guarantee is vacuous, because two producers derive different ids for one logical analysis and the database gets two rows where both PRDs promise one.
  record_id = sha256( lower(kind) + NUL + lower(subject) + NUL + canonical_json(significant_params) ).hexdigest()
  canonical_json sorts keys and uses compact separators. Truncate to 32 chars for DISPLAY ONLY, never for identity.
  significant_params is supplied by the CALLER per kind and is NEVER a table inside this module -- a per-kind map here would make the module domain-aware and would have to be edited every time either app adds a kind. The examples below are what one consumer will pass, recorded so the helper's shape is unambiguous; they are NOT to be hardcoded. For the annotation kinds: kbdl.build_genome -> the source identity; kbdl.annotation -> method, method_version, and the reference-data parameters that change the result (bakta_db for BAKTA; kofam_profiles and kofam_profile_set for KOFAMSCAN) -- two runs of the same method against different databases are DIFFERENT analyses and must not collide; kbdl.skani -> the SKANI database identity and version.
ARTIFACT URI SCHEME: values in the artifacts dict are restricted to EXACTLY three forms -- a bare absolute path, file://, or obj://<object_id> for the KBDL object store. Reject anything else. Without a fixed vocabulary, each app holds refs it cannot resolve the first time one arc carries both apps' kinds.


*** DECIDED IN CONFRONT ROUND 1 (task-adedb702). IMPLEMENT THESE; DO NOT RE-DERIVE. ***
S4/S7 THE PAYLOAD AND DETAIL WRITE PATH -- THIS FIXES A REAL CONTRADICTION IN THE SPEC YOU WERE GIVEN. AnalysisRecord carried a `payload`, the DDL had no payload column, read_detail read a subject_detail table, and record_analysis had no way to write one. Resolved:
  - TABLE runs GAINS: payload TEXT NULL -- the record's own opaque payload, which is SMALL (an objective value, a count, a status detail). Still never interpreted here.
  - THE SIGNATURE BECOMES: record_analysis(project, arc, record: AnalysisRecord, detail: dict | None = None) -> None. When detail is given it is written to subject_detail.detail_json for that record_id. This is ADDITIVE -- every existing call site stays correct.
  - THE SUMMARY COLUMNS (subject_feature_count, method_count, consistency_overall, consistency_metric_version, ic_corpus_version) ARE OPTIONAL FIELDS ON AnalysisRecord, SUPPLIED BY THE PRODUCER. This module COMPUTES NONE OF THEM -- it is domain-agnostic and has no idea what a feature or a consistency figure is. A record omitting them stores NULL.
S5 WHAT MAKES A KIND 'UNKNOWN' -- AND THE MODULE HOLDS NO LIST OF KINDS. Well-formed means matching ^[a-z0-9_]+(\.[a-z0-9_]+)+$ (a namespace plus at least one segment). A MALFORMED kind sets unknown_kind=1. If the caller passes known_kinds to the constructor, a well-formed kind OUTSIDE that set also sets unknown_kind=1. Either way the record is STORED AND COUNTED, never refused. DO NOT add a register_kind() API and DO NOT hardcode a kind list -- an adversary recommended both and they were rejected: a kind registry inside this module is exactly the domain knowledge it is forbidden to hold, for the same reason significant_params is caller-supplied.
S6 UPSERT SEMANTICS ON record_id: overwrite every mutable field (status, producer, producer_version, trust_tier, provenance, contract_version, artifacts, payload, the summary columns, and the detail blob WHEN ONE IS SUPPLIED); PRESERVE the original created_at; set updated_at to now UTC. A re-record supplying no detail LEAVES THE EXISTING BLOB IN PLACE rather than deleting it.
S8 artifacts IS dict[str, str] -- a caller-chosen name mapped to a URI. An adversary proposed list[{name, uri}]; REJECTED, the shape was already specified as a dict and changing it would break an agreed interface. file:// and file:/// are both ACCEPTED on read and normalised to file:// plus an absolute path on write.
S9 status IS EXACTLY ONE OF ok, failed, partial, lower-case. Any other value INCLUDING A CASE VARIANT is REJECTED. An adversary proposed accepting case-insensitively and coercing; rejected for consistency -- this module rejects a bad artifact URI and a missing provenance rather than repairing them.
S10 DATABASE PATH AND THE READ/WRITE ASYMMETRY: create the PARENT DIRECTORY of db_path if missing. On any WRITE error, log a warning on a NAMED LOGGER with a STABLE, GREPPABLE MESSAGE PREFIX, increment an in-process counter the caller can read, and RETURN. On a READ against a database that cannot be opened, RAISE. These are deliberately different: a failed write must not break a pipeline, but a failed read masquerading as 'no data' is precisely the confusion the no-hardcoded-fallback rule exists to prevent.


*** REVIEW ROUND 1 -- CHRIS REVERSED THE IDENTITY MODEL. THIS SUPERSEDES ANY EARLIER STATEMENT IN THIS PROMPT ABOUT record_id. READ IT BEFORE YOU IMPLEMENT ANYTHING. ***
Chris, 2026-09-24, verbatim: "No - it should not, so runs should be dated and ideally grouped in the interace, and critically you should be able to 'delete' a run from the database if you decide for example that an older run isn't useful. The apps should offer this kind of delete interface and the underlying data API should support it."

RE-RUNS MUST NOT COLLAPSE. The earlier spec derived ONE record_id from kind + subject + significant_params, so a second run of an identical analysis replaced its predecessor. That is the collapse he rejects. IDENTITY IS NOW SPLIT:

  analysis_id = sha256( lower(kind) + NUL + lower(subject) + NUL + canonical_json(significant_params) ).hexdigest()
  record_id   = sha256( analysis_id + NUL + run_uid ).hexdigest()

  - analysis_id IS EXACTLY THE OLD record_id DERIVATION, UNCHANGED. Only its JOB changed: it GROUPS every run of one logical analysis instead of collapsing them. It is still produced by ONE shared helper in this module.
  - record_id is the per-RUN primary key. run_uid is REQUIRED on AnalysisRecord -- do NOT default it to a fresh uuid4, because that would quietly make every retry a new row. A producer that mints run_uid once at run start and reuses it on retry gets idempotency; one that mints a fresh id per attempt gets a row per attempt, by its own visible choice.
  - THE RETRY GUARANTEE SURVIVES UNCHANGED: re-recording the SAME record_id (same run_uid) still REPLACES. What changed is that a RE-RUN is a different run_uid, hence a different record_id, hence a new dated row.

DDL CHANGES:
  - TABLE runs GAINS: analysis_id TEXT NOT NULL, run_uid TEXT NOT NULL.
  - INDEX on (analysis_id, created_at DESC). Without it, "the runs of this analysis, newest first" -- the query the grouped interface issues -- is a full scan.
  - TABLE subject_detail stays keyed by record_id, so two runs of one analysis hold TWO blobs and deleting one leaves the other.
  - analysis_id and run_uid are IMMUTABLE. A write that changes either on an existing record_id is a different record and must be REJECTED, not silently applied.

INTERFACE CHANGES, all ADDITIVE -- every call site written against the agreed interface stays correct:
  record_analysis(project, arc, record: AnalysisRecord, detail: dict | None = None) -> None
  list_analyses(project, arc, kind: str | None = None, analysis_id: str | None = None, latest_only: bool = False) -> list[AnalysisRecord]
  delete_record(record_id: str) -> bool

  - latest_only returns exactly ONE row per analysis_id, the newest by created_at.
  - delete_record is a HARD delete of the runs row, CASCADING to its subject_detail blob. No tombstone -- this is a per-user curation store and the independent evidence that the work happened is the runs tree and trace.jsonl, which this module cannot touch. Deleting an id that does not exist returns False and IS NOT AN ERROR; a delete is a thing a person does twice by accident.

TESTS THIS ADDS (all in the contract suite, so they run against the real store AND the fake): a second run with a new run_uid producing a SECOND row rather than replacing; both rows sharing one analysis_id; a retry with the SAME run_uid still replacing; latest_only returning one newest row per analysis_id; the index existing; delete_record removing row AND blob and returning True; delete_record on an absent id returning False without raising; deleting one run of two leaving the other and its blob intact; a write changing analysis_id or run_uid on an existing record_id REJECTED; and a record with no run_uid REJECTED rather than defaulted.


*** DECIDED IN CONFRONT ROUND 2 (task-94a4bb21). PIN THESE EXACTLY. ***
S17 AnalysisRecord IS FROZEN WITH TYPES: record_id:str, analysis_id:str, run_uid:str, kind:str, created_at:str, producer:str, producer_version:str, subject:str, status:Literal['ok','failed','partial'], artifacts:dict[str,str], payload:dict|None, trust_tier:Literal['verified','homology','hypothesis','opinion'], provenance:dict, contract_version:int, subject_feature_count:int|None, method_count:int|None, consistency_overall:float|None, consistency_metric_version:str|None, ic_corpus_version:str|None.
S18 canonical_json IS LOAD-BEARING -- the identity model rests on two producers hashing byte-identical input. RFC 8259, UTF-8, keys sorted by CODE POINT, separators (',',':'), NO whitespace, strings NFC-normalised, NUL is U+0000.
  *** FLOAT VALUES IN significant_params ARE REJECTED (code bad_float_param). *** Permitted: str, int, bool, None, and lists/dicts of those. An adversary recommended specifying a float FORMAT instead; that was REJECTED because pinning a format does not stop 0.1+0.2, a JSON round-trip and another language's parser differing in the last bit while every producer believes it complies. A producer with a float parameter formats it to a string itself and is thereby forced to choose the precision that matters.
S19 ARTIFACT URIs, pinned: absolute POSIX path ^/ ; file:// accepted as file:// OR file:/// on read and normalised to file:// plus an absolute path on write; obj://<object_id> with object_id matching ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$. Anything else raises RecordValidationError(code=bad_artifact_uri).
S21 FAIL-SOFT INSTRUMENTATION, named so tests can assert it: logger 'kbutillib.koros_arc_store'; every soft-failed write logs at WARNING with prefix 'koros_arc_store_write_soft_fail:'; count readable as KorosArcStore.failed_write_count.
S22 DB PATH PRECEDENCE: constructor db_path, else $KBDL_RUN_DB when set and non-empty, else ~/.kbdl/runs.sqlite. Failure to create the parent directory is a WRITE failure and takes the soft-fail path; a READ against an unopenable database still RAISES.
S23 known_kinds: constructor argument, set[str]|None, IMMUTABLE for the store's lifetime, checked at record_analysis only.
S24 DELETE IS ONE TRANSACTION: BEGIN IMMEDIATE; DELETE FROM subject_detail WHERE record_id=?; DELETE FROM runs WHERE record_id=?; COMMIT. Return True when the runs delete affected a row. MANUAL cascade, NOT an FK pragma -- behaviour must not depend on a PRAGMA foreign_keys setting a caller may not have applied.
S25 latest_only TIE-BREAK: created_at DESC, then updated_at DESC, then record_id DESC. Two runs can share a timestamp and the answer must still be deterministic.
S26 provenance TYPES: bridge_kind:str required, one of the five permitted values; metric:{name:str, value:int|float|str, units:str|None}; source:{db:str, accession:str}|None.
S29 PAYLOAD SIZE -- DO NOT REJECT. A payload over 64KB LOGS A WARNING naming the record and its size and IS STORED ANYWAY. An adversary recommended rejecting over 64KB; REJECTED, because the write path fails soft, so a rejected write is logged and DROPPED -- a producer whose payload innocently grew would lose records silently. The limit is a smell to surface, not a gate. Same for detail blobs: NO cap, the blob tier exists to hold large things.
S31 STATUS TRANSITIONS ARE UNCONSTRAINED -- any status may replace any other on the same record_id, INCLUDING failed -> ok. An adversary wanted to constrain them; REJECTED, because a retry exists precisely to turn a failed run into an ok one.
S32 TIMESTAMPS: ISO 8601 UTC, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ, literal Z, never an offset. The store generates updated_at; created_at comes from the producer and is VALIDATED against that format (code bad_timestamp).
S34 FILTER PRECEDENCE: kind and analysis_id combine CONJUNCTIVELY; latest_only applies AFTER filtering; ordering per S25.
S35 subject IS STORED VERBATIM. lower(subject) appears ONLY inside the hash derivation. A builder who lowercases the stored subject hands every consumer mangled identifiers -- test for it.
S36 PRAGMAS: journal_mode=WAL at initialisation. The access pattern is a KBDL client writing while a dashboard reads, and the rollback journal blocks exactly that. Create the (analysis_id, created_at DESC) index at initialisation too.

Without a fake shipped from here, each writes its own, and a consumer-written fake drifts toward whatever makes the consumer's tests pass -- the divergence then surfaces at integration time, in a third repo, as somebody else's build breaking. A PERMISSIVE FAKE IS WORSE THAN NO FAKE: it lets a consumer's tests pass against behaviour the real store rejects.

DELIVERABLE 1 -- `kbutillib.koros_arc_store_testing`, a SEPARATE module so that importing the store never drags a test double into production code.
